recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed for FHIR-14175 unless the Security WG makes a new decision to rename the established targetFormat/sigFormat elements or change their MIME bindings.
issue_request: FHIR-14175 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 FHIR-core Security WG issue requesting that Signature distinguish the MIME type of the signature blob from the MIME format of the signed FHIR resources by renaming the old contentType field and adding a separate signed-resource format field.
initial_application: Git commit f72fd6237875c6ba9d2a21e235881c7fed559700 appears to be the original GF#14175 application: it changed the Signature datatype source from Signature.contentType to Signature.targetFormat and Signature.sigFormat, bound both rows to MimeType, described targetFormat as the technical format of the signed resources, and updated Provenance signature examples. Later commit b96bbd292505dde0f56bdda132c7476d85b19de8 renamed Signature.blob to Signature.data without undoing the targetFormat/sigFormat split.
additional_context: Signature is active in the current build through source/fhir.ini and is marked normative. Later reconciliations for FHIR-48679 and FHIR-47211 are already on the combined branch and refine adjacent MIME/canonicalization wording while preserving the FHIR-14175 distinction between targetFormat and sigFormat.
reconciliation: No source change was made because source/datatypes/signature.xml already defines Signature.targetFormat for the signed resources and Signature.sigFormat for the signature itself, both bound to MimeType, and current examples/rules use targetFormat and sigFormat without stale Signature.contentType references.

related_jiras.note: Renamed Signature.blob to Signature.data after the FHIR-14175 split, leaving targetFormat/sigFormat intact.
Scoped short-form xml/json/ttl MIME allowances away from Signature.targetFormat and is already represented on the combined branch.
Corrected later signature-rule wording to use sigFormat/targetFormat consistently and is already represented on the combined branch.
